name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 236 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 236 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Violence has intensified in Manipur with gunmen killing four Naga civilians on the Imphal-Ukhrul highway, a sniper killing four Tangkhul Nagas on the same route, and suspected militants opening fire on two vehicles in Ukhrul, killing four travelers; in Kangpokpi district a woman farmer was killed and three men wounded, and a bandh over the killing of a Kuki woman disrupted normal life. In Kashmir security forces conducted a joint mock drill in Bandipora’s Hajin area and placed forces on high alert after two SPOs were killed in Kishtwar. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Volden har økt i Manipur etter at væpnede menn drepte fire Naga-sivile på Imphal-Ukhrul-veien, en snikskytter drepte fire Tangkhul-Nagas på samme rute, og mistenkte militante åpnet ild mot to kjøretøy i Ukhrul, hvor fire reisende ble drept; i Kangpokpi-distrikt ble en kvinnelig bonde drept og tre menn såret, og en streik som følge av drapet på en Kuki-kvinne forstyrret hverdagen. I Kashmir gjennomførte sikkerhetsstyrkene en felles øvelsesøvelse i Bandiporas Hajin-område og satte styrkene på høy beredskap etter at to SPO-er ble drept i Kishtwar. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
